citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., and Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. In Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pages 1525–1534, Berlin, Germany.
creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández (CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam)
description: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) is a dataset to evaluate computational models for text understanding via a word prediction task. It is a collection of narrative passages (from the BookCorpus) where human subjects can guess the last word when exposed to the whole passage, but not when only seeing the last sentence. The dataset consists of 10,022 passages (4,869 development and 5,153 test) requiring models to track information across broad discourse context.
name: LAMBADA
publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 subjects judged each item in the broad-context condition (steps 1 and 2), and up to 10 subjects judged each item in the sentence-only condition (step 3).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-step crowdsourcing pipeline was used: (1) One human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage (context + target sentence); if correct, (2) a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if also correct, (3) additional subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or 10 unsuccessful guesses were reached. Subjects in step 3 were allowed 3 guesses per sentence. The same subject could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions. Passages were included in LAMBADA only if no subject in step 3 could guess the target word.
rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA (48% of target words) compared to the input data distribution, while verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are underrepresented. More than 80% of LAMBADA passages include the target word in the context (vs. less than 15% in the unfiltered input data). LAMBADA items contain quoted direct speech significantly more often than input items overall (71% vs. 61%). The use of unpublished novels from BookCorpus was intentional to minimize the usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources, in contrast to news data, Wikipedia, or famous novels.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from the BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels. After duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material, the corpus contained 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions. Passages were filtered using a combination of four language models (a pre-trained RNN and three models trained on BookCorpus: a 4-gram model, an RNN, and a feed-forward model) to exclude passages where the target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any model. Remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower crowdsourcing in a three-step pipeline: (1) one subject guessed the target word from the whole passage; (2) if correct, a second subject also guessed from the whole passage; (3) if also correct, additional subjects tried to guess from the target sentence only (up to 10 unsuccessful guesses). Only passages passing all three steps were included. About 1 in 25 input examples passed all selection steps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing 5,325 unpublished novels and 465 million words after duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material with a stop word list.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is heavily skewed toward proper nouns (48% of target words) and common nouns (37%), with verbs, adjectives, and adverbs underrepresented. The strict hit-or-miss approach (requiring exact word match) excludes passages where subjects provided plausible synonymous continuations. The evaluation performed in the paper is described as preliminary and a proof-of-concept study. Standard language models are bound to fail on LAMBADA by design, as one of the first filters was to choose passages where simple language models failed to predict the upcoming word.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The BookCorpus was preprocessed by removing duplicates and filtering potentially offensive material using a stop word list. Passages were constructed with a context of minimum complete sentences cumulatively containing at least 50 tokens before the target sentence. Novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions (2,662 novels for training, encompassing 203 million words; the remainder for dev+test). Automated language model filtering excluded passages where the target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of four language models.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus were made available at http://clic.cimec.unitn.it/lambada/. The test set was to be made available at the time of a planned public competition.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote research in language understanding by providing a challenging benchmark that exposes the limitations of current language models in tracking broad discourse context. The authors plan to announce a public competition based on the LAMBADA data to stimulate the development of novel language models.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating computational models for text understanding, specifically their ability to track information across broad discourse context for word prediction. Intended as a challenging benchmark for language models and to encourage development of models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text. The development set can be used to fine-tune models to the specifics of LAMBADA passages.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models were used to filter passages: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) (Mikolov et al., 2011), a standard 4-gram model trained on BookCorpus, an RNN trained on BookCorpus, and a feed-forward model trained on BookCorpus. Passages where the target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of these models were excluded.
